$comment: Central physics collision layer matrix. See docs/tdd/90-source-reconciliation.md C15 and docs/adr/0003-physics-ownership.md. Governed by project/Config/Schema/layers.schema.json and validated by tools/validation/validate_registries.py. Index 0 is reserved: AzPhysics::CollisionLayer::Default is index 0, and CollisionLayers::GetLayer(name) returns Default when a name is not found (verified in the engine source at tag 2605.0, Code/Framework/AzFramework/AzFramework/Physics/Collision/CollisionLayers.h). A typo'd layer name therefore does not error at runtime, it silently puts the collider on Default. That is the defect this registry exists to prevent.

layers.name: Default
layers.description: Engine-reserved fallback. Nothing in Phoenix is authored onto this layer; a collider that lands here is a missing or misspelled layer assignment, so it is deliberately given no collision partners and shows up as an object that falls through the world.

layers.name: StaticWorld
layers.description: Non-moving level geometry. Owns the collision the character controller sweeps against.

layers.name: DynamicWorld
layers.description: Physics-driven movable objects. Server-authoritative and never client-predicted, per docs/tdd/04-multiplayer.md: PhysX is not deterministic, so a predicted rigid body would diverge.

layers.name: Character
layers.description: PhysX 5 character controllers for both player and AI characters.

layers.name: Trigger
layers.description: Non-blocking objective and script volumes. Reports overlap only; never pushes a character.

layers.name: HitQuery
layers.description: Query-only layer used by server-side hit resolution. Nothing is authored onto it; it exists so hit queries select a different set from the character controller's movement sweep.

layers.name: AIPerception
layers.description: Query-only layer for line-of-sight and cover checks, so perception does not pay for trigger volumes.

layers.name: Debug
layers.description: Development visualisation bodies. Collides with nothing, and is excluded from release builds by the feature flag in PhoenixFeatureFlags.
